raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Enable producer-only MRV2 prefill context parallelism for Mooncake by selecting PCP0 as the sender for each replicated TP/PP KV shard. Preserve all-worker save completion so a non-sending replica does not break connector composition.

## Claims

- Only PCP0 owns the producer bootstrap/listener/transfer path; replicas do not register duplicate TP/PP identities or send duplicate KV.
- All workers report delayed-save completion. Noncanonical ranks acknowledge only final block-bearing metadata, not the earlier allocation announcement; polling consumes that completion once.
- Producer PCP requires DCP=1. Consumers and `kv_both` require PCP=1. The documented setup uses PP=1 and DP=1.
- No model, attention kernel, scheduler, or replay workaround is included.

## Validation

Candidate: `02aa7f861148d9b776fa7fa3889ea4607f85804e`, based on `db3b0f0fae4bc98492b3863685e541e62bc59576`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py -q

# Three NVIDIA GPUs, Mooncake CUDA13 installed; the test pins its tiny MLA model.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/test_pcp.py -v -s
```

- Units: **168 passed**, 41 warnings, exit 0, 81.49s.
- New real OpenAI-server regression: **1 passed**, 2 warnings, exit 0, 67.58s. Checks single bootstrap ownership, repeated concurrent/chunked P/D generation, and external-cache token adoption. Uses the repository's existing `check_logprobs_close`; it does not require bitwise invariance across execution layouts.
- The same new test on base `db3b0f0fae` fails during producer startup: both PCP ranks attempt the bootstrap bind, producing `[Errno 98] Address already in use` (**1 failed**, 39.45s).
- Ruff 0.14.0 and diff checks passed. Added the regression to the existing NVIDIA nightly Mooncake CI step; CI execution is pending.

Additional clean serving smoke: 3 H20 GPUs, `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` revision `85864749cd611b4353ce1decdb286193298f64c7`, P TP1/PCP2/DCP1, D TP1/PCP1/DCP1, PP1/DP1, same Pod, Mooncake TCP, eager, block64, chunk256, no prefix caching. Four prompts (including a 1290-token chunked prompt) and 16 requests at concurrency4, with 32 generated tokens each:

| Check | BF16 | FP16 |
|---|---:|---:|
| P/D requests completed | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| Exact sequential output vs standalone | 3/4 | 4/4 |
| Exact concurrent output vs sequential P/D | 16/16 | 15/16 |
| Existing logprobs compatibility checker, separate clean run | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| External cached-token delta | 6600 | 6600 |
| Requests sent by PCP0 / PCP1 | 20 / 0 | 20 / 0 |
| D KV usage after requests | 0 | 0 |

Strict text-invariance checks remain **FAIL** and are retained separately from the compatibility checks. The 16B smoke used `d66541141a`; subsequent changes only add tests/CI, and the connector source SHA256 is identical at the final candidate. The real-entry regression and unit suite were rerun from the exact final remote commit/package.

The BF16 long-input discrepancy is precision/execution-shape sensitive: fixed-prefix probes match the baseline next token at 11/12 points; the initial point ties its top two scores. PCP replicas contain identical KV across all 27 layers. A separate transfer readback confirmed matching source/destination bytes for the original long request. FP16 and a diagnostic 16-token aligned tail recomputation restore its initial token. These observations support numerical-path sensitivity; they do not identify a specific faulty operator or certify general model accuracy. Diagnostic hooks/replay changes are excluded from the delivery source and clean smoke runs.

This is a correctness/compatibility smoke, not a performance benchmark or a validation of GLM-5.2 FP8, cross-node RDMA, large heterogeneous TP, PP>1, DP>1, or GPU MultiConnector+offload.

## Details

With DCP1, MRV2 gathers the latent KV before cache insertion, so PCP ranks at the same TP/PP position retain replicated logical KV. Mooncake discovery identifies DP/TP/PP workers without a PCP coordinate. Letting every replica register/send therefore collides on ownership and duplicates transport.

The completion lifecycle is separate from sender ownership:

1. Scheduler allocation announces a transfer with empty blocks; replicas must not acknowledge completion yet.
2. Final block-bearing metadata follows producer completion and requests delayed block release. Noncanonical replicas acknowledge this metadata once; PCP0 retains responsibility for the actual transfer.
3. D requests KV from the canonical worker. The scheduler waits for all local worker completions before freeing the producer's blocks.

The default world-size completion protocol follows the composability invariant in merged NIXL [#53903](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53903). Dynamic remote fan-out/fan-in accounting remains unchanged.

Duplicate/reuse checks: ordinary Mooncake PCP remains tracked in [#60523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523); [#61974](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61974) excludes PCP; [#45340](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45340) addresses aligned CP-sharded layouts rather than this asymmetric replicated producer setup. [#62916](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62916) separately addresses multi-node PCP engine-ID synchronization. None replaces this ownership change.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests, and this description. Human review and confirmation of the submitted scope/results remain required before requesting re-review.

I think the bootstrap 503 and retry mechanism introduced here is somewhat redundant. Even without PCP, the original bootstrap server already has the potential issue of incomplete dp/tp/pp registration. In my original design, this was guarded by querying the /health endpoint (see [examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py:43](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py#L43)). I'm not familiar with the vllm-router project, but if vllm-router doesn't already handle this, I believe the right fix would be to submit a PR to vllm-router to address it there, rather than re-introducing topology completeness checks on the decoder side.

nodes.body:
Yes, I think we can rely on pcp_rank > 0 not participating in KV sending here. In the merged MRV2 PCP implementation [#46570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46570), PCP splits the prefill computation, but the latent K/V is all-gathered across the PCP group before cache insertion. So the PCP ranks end up holding replicated copies of the same logical KV cache. Having the other PCP ranks send as well would just duplicate the transfer and completion notification, which is why we use pcp_rank == 0 as the canonical sender for each TP/PP shard.

My understanding is that `need_send` and `pull_tasks_count` are mainly about dynamic remote fan-out and fan-in, especially for heterogeneous TP/PP. We could account for PCP there, but both paths would then need special handling for the non-sending PCP replicas, and it would mix local ownership with remote transfer topology. Using `get_finished_count()` to express the number of local workers that can actually report finished_sending seems a bit clearer, so the producer count becomes world_size / pcp_size.

+### MRV2 prefill context parallelism
+
+With model runner V2, a `kv_producer` can use
+`--prefill-context-parallel-size` with a supported MLA model and attention
+backend. The producer must use `--decode-context-parallel-size 1` so that
+PCP ranks at each TP/PP position hold replicated KV caches. Only PCP rank 0
+registers as a sender and transfers KV; all workers report save completion
+before the scheduler frees the request's blocks.
+
+The decoder must use `--prefill-context-parallel-size 1`. PCP greater than 1
+is rejected for `kv_consumer` and `kv_both`, and for producers using DCP
+greater than 1. Use PP=1 and DP=1 for this producer-only PCP setup; other
+PP/DP combinations require separate validation.
+
 ## Environment Variables

@@ -0,0 +1,169 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Producer-only PCP over real Mooncake TCP transport; requires three GPUs."""
+
+import concurrent.futures
+import json
+import os
+import uuid
+
+import pytest
+import requests
+
+from tests.models.utils import check_logprobs_close
+from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_ports_list
+
+
+@pytest.mark.distributed
+def test_pcp_producer_transfers_replicated_kv():
+    """One sender must serve chunked requests without falling back to prefill."""
+    model = os.environ.get(
+        "MOONCAKE_PCP_TEST_MODEL", "hmellor/tiny-random-DeepseekV2ForCausalLM"
+    )
+    prefill_port, decode_port, bootstrap_port = get_open_ports_list(3)
+    args = [
+        "--served-model-name",
+        "pcp-test",
+        "--host",
+        "127.0.0.1",
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--dtype",
+        "bfloat16",
+        "--enforce-eager",
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "2048",
+        "--max-num-batched-tokens",
+        "256",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "8",
+        "--block-size",
+        "64",
+        "--num-gpu-blocks-override",
+        "128",
+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.65",
+        "--no-enable-prefix-caching",
+    ]
+    if model == "hmellor/tiny-random-DeepseekV2ForCausalLM":
+        args += ["--revision", "c0146ef3550ef77c6520211184cf41184b92346a"]
+    env = {"VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER": "1", "MC_FORCE_TCP": "1"}
+    producer = json.dumps(
+        {
+            "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector",
+            "kv_role": "kv_producer",
+            "kv_connector_extra_config": {"mooncake_protocol": "tcp"},
+        }
+    )
+    consumer = json.dumps(
+        {
+            "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector",
+            "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
+            "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail",
+            "kv_connector_extra_config": {"mooncake_protocol": "tcp"},
+        }
+    )
+    with (
+        RemoteOpenAIServer(
+            model,
+            args
+            + [
+                "--port",
+                str(prefill_port),
+                "--prefill-context-parallel-size",
+                "2",
+                "--kv-transfer-config",
+                producer,
+            ],
+            auto_port=False,
+            env_dict=env
+            | {
+                "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "0,1",
+                "VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT": str(bootstrap_port),
+            },
+        ) as prefill,
+        RemoteOpenAIServer(
+            model,
+            args + ["--port", str(decode_port), "--kv-transfer-config", consumer],
+            auto_port=False,
+            env_dict=env | {"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "2"},
+        ) as decode,
+        prefill.get_client() as p_client,
+        decode.get_client() as d_client,
+    ):
+        bootstrap = f"http://127.0.0.1:{bootstrap_port}"
+        response = requests.get(f"{bootstrap}/query", timeout=10)
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        info = response.json()
+        assert list(info) == ["0"]
+        assert set(info["0"]["worker_addr"]) == {"0"}
+        assert set(info["0"]["worker_addr"]["0"]) == {"0"}
+
+        def complete(client, prompt, params=None, max_tokens=16):
+            return client.completions.create(
+                model="pcp-test",
+                prompt=prompt,
+                max_tokens=max_tokens,
+                temperature=0,
+                seed=42,
+                logprobs=5,
+                extra_body={
+                    "ignore_eos": True,
+                    "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True,
+                    "kv_transfer_params": params,
+                },
+            )
+
+        def disaggregated(prompt):
+            transfer_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
+            complete(
+                p_client,
+                prompt,
+                {"do_remote_decode": True, "transfer_id": transfer_id},
+                max_tokens=1,
+            )
+            return complete(
+                d_client,
+                prompt,
+                {
+                    "do_remote_prefill": True,
+                    "remote_bootstrap_addr": bootstrap,
+                    "remote_engine_id": info["0"]["engine_id"],
+                    "transfer_id": transfer_id,
+                },
+            )
+
+        def hits():

inline_comments.body: I think the bootstrap 503 and retry mechanism introduced here is somewhat redundant. Even without PCP, the original bootstrap server already has the potential issue of incomplete dp/tp/pp registration. In my original design, this was guarded by querying the /health endpoint (see [examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py:43](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py#L43)). I'm not familiar with the vllm-router project, but if vllm-router doesn't already handle this, I believe the right fix would be to submit a PR to vllm-router to address it there, rather than re-introducing topology completeness checks on the decoder side.

However, if we can guarantee that ranks with pcp > 0 never participate in sending, then a global static configuration is indeed a better approach.

inline_comments.body:
Yes, I think we can rely on pcp_rank > 0 not participating in KV sending here. In the merged MRV2 PCP implementation [#46570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46570), PCP splits the prefill computation, but the latent K/V is all-gathered across the PCP group before cache insertion. So the PCP ranks end up holding replicated copies of the same logical KV cache. Having the other PCP ranks send as well would just duplicate the transfer and completion notification, which is why we use pcp_rank == 0 as the canonical sender for each TP/PP shard.

My understanding is that `need_send` and `pull_tasks_count` are mainly about dynamic remote fan-out and fan-in, especially for heterogeneous TP/PP. We could account for PCP there, but both paths would then need special handling for the non-sending PCP replicas, and it would mix local ownership with remote transfer topology. Using `get_finished_count()` to express the number of local workers that can actually report finished_sending seems a bit clearer, so the producer count becomes world_size / pcp_size.
